title: Jiminy Glick in LaLaWood
full_review:
Martin Short's lame improvised comedy "Jiminy Glick in LaLaWood" (MGM) is short on laughs, short on plot and short on reasons why it is worth seeing.

In fact, the only thing it has in excess is crass jokes about the titular talk-show host's sex life.

Based on Comedy Central's TV show "Primetime Glick," the film orbits around a clueless entertainment critic (a well-padded Short), who is rocketed into the showbiz spotlight when he lands an exclusive one-on-one with a notoriously reclusive young megastar (Corey Pearson), while at the same time becoming involved in a Hollywood murder mystery surrounding a disappeared starlet (Elizabeth Perkins).

Despite some amusing mock interviews with real celebrities, director Vadim Jean's unnecessarily crude and mostly unfunny effort is another example of taking a TV comedy skit and pointlessly stretching it into a feature-length film, here saddled with a silly whodunit subplot.

The film contains lewd sexual situations and humor, including a spoof lesbian love scene, brief violence and recurring rough and vulgar language and profanity. The USCCB Office for Film & Broadcasting classification is L -- limited adult audience, films whose problematic content many adults would find troubling. The Motion Picture Association of America rating is R -- restricted.
